To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the SSBH56KQ110L and SSBKQ76L mutant proteins form tetramers that are more stable than the SSBH5SK mutant protein.
the SSB protein from Eschericia coli forms a homotetramer and that the amino acids at position 55 and 76 are important for stabilizing the tetrameric structure of the protein.
mutations at position 76 and 110, which stabilize the tetrameric form of the E. coli single‐stranded DNA binding (SSb) protein, are also able to stabilize the tetramers of the SSBH 55K single mutant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the histidine at the subunit–subunit interface of the SSB protein and the role of the glutamine at the C‐terminal region of the protein in the tetrameric stability of the SSBH protein.
the identification of amino acids that are important for the stability of the E. coli SSB tetrameric structure.
the role of the histidine at 55 and the glutamines at 76 and 110 in the stability of the SSB tetramer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the histidine at 55, which is present at the subunits interface of the tetramer, is essential for tetramer formation and stability and that the amino acids at positions 76 and 110, located at the subunit‐subunit interface, contribute to the stability of the tetramers.
the histidine at 55 is important for stabilizing the subunit interactions of SSB protein, while the glutamine at 110 and 76 are involved in stabilizing the SSB tetramer.

the histidine at 55 is the most important amino acid in the SSB subunit interface and that the histidine 55‐glutamine 76 and histidine 55 ‐glutamine 110 contacts are the most important of the subunit interface contacts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SSBH56K mutation destabilizes tetramer formation by weakening the interaction between the H55 side‐chain and the Q76 or Q110 side‐chain.
the SSBH protein is stabilized by the interaction between histidine at position H55 with the glutamine side chains at positions 76 and 110.
mutations which stabilize the subunit interface in the SSB tetramer also stabilize the tetramer itself.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SSBH56KQ76L, SSBH55KYQ76L, and SSBH56KYQ110L mutants are the most stable SSB mutants characterized to date.

the stability of the tetramerization domain of SSB protein can be modulated by mutations at residues that are not part of the tetramer interface, and that these residues are located on the surface of the protein.
the histidine at the tetramer interface of the SSB tetramer plays an important role in the stability of the tetramers.
